title: Boyle's Law & Kinetic Molecular Theory
notes:
Boyle's Law

At constant temperature, the volume of a gas is inversely proportional to its pressure: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂

Mnemonic: P.I.G. V. K.I.R.E.

Particles, Identical, Gravity-free, Volume negligible, Kinetic energy constant, Instability, Random motion, Elastic collisions

The 8 Postulates of KMT

  • Tiny Particles — gases are made of extremely tiny molecules or atoms.
  • Identical Size & Shape — all molecules of a pure gas are identical.
  • No Force — no gravitational or intermolecular forces act between particles.
  • Negligible Volume — molecule volume is practically zero vs. the container.
  • Kinetic Energy — proportional to absolute temperature.
  • Perpetual Motion — molecules are never at rest.
  • Random Path — straight-line, zigzag motion between collisions.
  • Elastic Collisions — no kinetic energy lost in collisions.
